searchText: Has anyone synced a client with a ram-disk? Is disk still a bottleneck? What type of sync, and which client (execution vs consensus)? I'm guessing you mean execution client, and given the requirement of ramdisk I suspect that you are talking about some kind of fast/warp/quick/zippy/snappy/hyper sync (since the others would require a ridiculous amount of RAM)? Execution client. ramdisk would be for state access/storage and thus would need to be reasonably large. A pruned client I assume? I mean, with the instances amazon has available, I think an archive node is possible too. 24 TB of storage is enough, right? That should last for at least the next few months of state growth 🤣 What i found from running a node with ramdisk was that it didn't keep in sync better, or process blocks that much faster. The vast majority of state being executed is likely very warm in a variety of caches (both geth and Linux's fscache). However, what we DID find was that when simulating all transactions found on the wire, the distribution of time it took to simulate those transactions became MUCH more consistent than nodes that are backed by disk I had histogram of simulation time, the non-ramdisk nodes would have these massive outliers at like 100ms and beyond. the ramdisk node's histogram kept everything neatly packed in much, much smaller timeframe i can't remember exactly the times, but i remember the shape of that chart. Thanks, cool findings [Execution Specs] I am a bit occupied right now to work on the `chain runner`. Hence please feel free to pick it up if anyone is interested in the same. Thanks. Erigon archive takes a grand total of 1.5 TB Erigon's MDBX is memory mapped, so if you have 64 gigs of RAM, the plain state table is fully mapped Not sure if it's the same as ramdisk, but should be really close <@!301186049323958275> this should make you happy: https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/commit/d71c50f6564c1f7a73f09a20557084df9195679c Yes, very happy!
